subject: Music Production
title: Sam Phillips and the Birth of Rock
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Sam Phillips and the Birth of Rock.

hook.text: Sam Phillips opened a tiny Memphis studio in 1950, determined to record overlooked Black artists.

buildup.text: He captured raw blues and gospel performances that major labels considered too rough to release.

discovery.text: Phillips realized a white artist singing with that raw feel could break through racial barriers.

twist.text: A shy truck driver named Elvis Presley walked in and recorded a blues song his own wild way.

climax.text: That session launched rock and roll, and Sun Records became ground zero for a revolution.

punchline.text: A tiny Memphis studio ignited rock and roll.

quiz.question: What did Sam Phillips originally set out to record?
options: Overlooked Black blues and gospel artists
